name: How Much Space Does an ADU Need to Work Well?

mainEntity.name: How much space do I need for a legal-feeling custom ADU layout with kitchen and bath?
mainEntity.text: How much space do I need for a legal-feeling custom ADU layout with kitchen and bath?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU does not need to feel large to work well, but it does need enough space for safe circulation, storage, and usable kitchen and bathroom clearances. The best layouts make every square foot count by combining functions intelligently, such as using built-ins, compact appliances, and efficient plumbing placement. Even when the footprint is small, the design should preserve comfortable movement between the entry, kitchen, bath, and sleeping area. Homeowners should avoid layouts that technically fit on paper but feel cramped in daily use. A contractor and designer should coordinate early to make sure the plan supports furniture placement, appliance clearances, and code-sensitive spacing. Good space planning is often the difference between an ADU that feels rentable and one that feels awkward.
acceptedAnswer.description: A workable ADU layout depends on how efficiently the space is planned, but a kitchen, bathroom, sleeping area, and living zone all need enough room to function comfortably. Tight layouts can work if circulation, storage, and appliance clearances are handled carefully. The design should prioritize livability over simply fitting rooms inside the footprint.
